bankLabel: CompTIA A+ Core 2 (220-1202) PBQ Arena Production Campaign

missions.title: Choose the Deployment Realm
missions.objective: 220-1202 1.1–1.3 — OS types, installations, upgrades, and Windows editions
missions.briefing: Four users require platforms suited to different workloads.
instructions: Review every task.
Select the best response for each task.
Each correct task earns one point.

tasks.prompt: A kiosk runs one managed Windows application and must block unapproved software.
A design user needs domain join, BitLocker management, and Remote Desktop hosting.
A developer needs a Unix-like desktop with native Apple application testing.
A lab appliance needs a lightweight open-source server without a desktop.

explanations.task-1: Kiosk mode restricts the device to its assigned application.
explanations.task-2: Windows Pro supplies the requested business features.
explanations.task-3: macOS is required for native Apple platform development.
explanations.task-4: A minimal Linux server suits the headless open-source appliance.

missions.title: Equip the Windows Administration Bench
missions.briefing: A support team must open the correct Windows console for each request.
instructions: Review every task.
Select the best response for each task.
Each correct task earns one point.

tasks.prompt: Review recurring application errors and their timestamps.
Create and resize a local partition.
Create a program that runs every Friday evening.
Temporarily disable selected startup services for diagnosis.

explanations.task-1: Event Viewer exposes timestamped application logs.
explanations.task-2: Disk Management controls local volumes and partitions.
explanations.task-3: Task Scheduler launches programs on triggers.
explanations.task-4: System Configuration supports selective startup diagnosis.

missions.title: Command the Recovery Terminal
missions.briefing: Match each recovery need to the command that performs it most directly.
instructions: Review every task.
Select the best response for each task.
Each correct task earns one point.

tasks.prompt: Verify and repair protected Windows system files.
Inspect and repair file-system errors on a volume.
Display the current IP address, gateway, and DNS configuration.
Immediately refresh computer and user Group Policy.

explanations.task-1: SFC validates protected operating-system files.
explanations.task-2: CHKDSK checks a volume and its file system.
explanations.task-3: IPCONFIG displays Windows TCP/IP configuration.
explanations.task-4: GPUPDATE refreshes Group Policy.

missions.title: Configure the Branch Workstations
missions.briefing: Apply the approved Windows network profile, address method, sharing state, and remote-access setting.
instructions: Review each requirement.
Select every configuration field.
Each correct field earns partial credit.

tasks.label: Reception
tasks.prompt: Public-facing reception PC; DHCP; no sharing; no inbound remote desktop.

tasks.label: Accounting
tasks.prompt: Trusted domain PC; DHCP; approved file sharing; inbound remote desktop disabled.

tasks.label: Support lab
tasks.prompt: Isolated private lab; static address; approved sharing; inbound remote desktop enabled.

explanations.task-1: Public profile and disabled inbound services reduce reception exposure.
explanations.task-2: The domain profile permits centrally controlled sharing without unnecessary remote desktop.
explanations.task-3: The isolated support lab uses its approved static and remote-management configuration.

missions.title: Cross the Unix Toolchain
missions.objective: 220-1202 1.8–1.9 — macOS and Linux features and tools
missions.briefing: Identify the platform tool that best completes each administrative task.
instructions: Review every task.
Select the best response for each task.
Each correct task earns one point.

tasks.prompt: Install a signed macOS application package distributed as a disk image.
Change Linux file permissions using symbolic or octal modes.
Review macOS backup history created by the built-in backup utility.
Install a package from a Debian-family repository.

explanations.task-1: DMG files are commonly mounted to install macOS applications.
explanations.task-2: CHMOD changes Unix permission bits.
explanations.task-3: Time Machine is the built-in macOS backup system.
explanations.task-4: APT manages packages on Debian-family Linux systems.

missions.title: Approve the Application Caravan
missions.briefing: Categorize each deployment by its primary delivery or compatibility model.
instructions: Review every task.
Select the best response for each task.
Each correct task earns one point.

tasks.prompt: A graphics program runs locally and requires a supported GPU and operating-system version.
Staff use mail entirely through a managed browser subscription.
A legacy finance program runs only inside a maintained virtual machine.
A collaboration client stores synchronized working copies locally and in a cloud service.

explanations.task-1: Local applications must meet hardware and OS requirements.
explanations.task-2: A complete browser subscription is SaaS.
explanations.task-3: Virtualization isolates the legacy dependency.
explanations.task-4: A synchronization client maintains cloud and local copies.

missions.title: Migrate the Guild Workstations
missions.briefing: Sequence a managed migration while preserving data and network access.
instructions: Review every task.
Select the best response for each task.
Each correct task earns one point.

tasks.prompt: Inventory applications, verify compatibility, and document the rollback plan.
Back up user data and validate the backup.
Perform the approved operating-system installation or upgrade.
Install approved drivers, applications, updates, and network settings.
Validate user data, security controls, connectivity, and documentation.

explanations.task-1: Compatibility and rollback planning precede change.
explanations.task-2: A verified backup protects recoverability.
explanations.task-3: Installation follows preparation.
explanations.task-4: Required software and configuration restore function.

missions.title: Sort the Defensive Shields
missions.briefing: Classify each safeguard by its primary control family.
instructions: Review every task.
Select the best response for each task.
Each correct task earns one point.

tasks.prompt: A locked equipment room limits physical entry.
Multifactor authentication protects administrative sign-in.
A written onboarding process defines account approvals.
A badge reader records entry to a restricted workspace.

explanations.task-1: Locks are physical barriers.
explanations.task-2: MFA is a technical identity control.
explanations.task-3: Written approval workflow is administrative.
explanations.task-4: A badge reader is a physical access control supported by technology.

missions.title: Secure the Shared Workshop
missions.briefing: Configure account type, data protection, local access, and auditing for shared systems.
instructions: Review each requirement.
Select every configuration field.
Each correct field earns partial credit.

tasks.label: Front desk
tasks.prompt: Standard daily user; encrypted drive; no shared-folder modification; sign-in auditing enabled.

tasks.label: Technician
tasks.prompt: Standard daily user; encrypted drive; modify approved support share; sign-in auditing enabled.

tasks.label: Offline lab
tasks.prompt: Local administrator for isolated recovery work; encrypted drive; modify lab share; sign-in auditing enabled.

explanations.task-1: Least privilege, encryption, read-only access, and auditing suit the front desk.
explanations.task-2: The technician retains standard-user status while receiving only required share modification.
explanations.task-3: The isolated recovery role requires its approved local administrative access and auditing.

missions.title: Fortify the Artisan Wireless Network
missions.objective: 220-1202 2.3 and 2.10 — Wireless authentication and SOHO security
missions.briefing: Apply an approved security profile to three wireless networks.
instructions: Review each requirement.
Select every configuration field.
Each correct field earns partial credit.

tasks.label: Staff
tasks.prompt: Modern managed devices; strongest personal-mode encryption; client access to internal resources.

tasks.label: Guest
tasks.prompt: Internet-only visitors; modern encryption; wireless clients isolated from each other.

tasks.label: Legacy quarantine
tasks.prompt: Temporary incompatible device segment; separate SSID; no internal access; scheduled for removal.

explanations.task-1: Staff devices use WPA3 and the approved internal path.
explanations.task-2: Guest isolation and blocked internal access separate visitors.
explanations.task-3: The quarantined legacy SSID uses its strongest compatible security and strict isolation.

missions.title: Identify the Human Threats
missions.briefing: Classify the primary threat shown by each original incident.
instructions: Review every task.
Select the best response for each task.
Each correct task earns one point.

tasks.prompt: A caller claims to be an executive and demands an urgent password reset.
A document macro encrypts accessible files and demands payment.
A message directs an employee to a cloned sign-in page.
A free utility silently records keyboard input.

explanations.task-1: Voice impersonation is vishing.
explanations.task-2: File encryption plus extortion indicates ransomware.
explanations.task-3: A deceptive credential page delivered by message is phishing.
explanations.task-4: Silent keystroke capture is keylogging.

missions.title: Purge the Infected Workstation
missions.briefing: Order the approved malware-removal process.
instructions: Review every task.
Select the best response for each task.
Each correct task earns one point.

tasks.prompt: Investigate symptoms and verify the malware indicators.
Quarantine the system and disable restore points when required by procedure.
Update protection tools and run approved removal scans.
Remediate remaining damage, update the operating system, and re-enable protection.
Verify normal operation, educate the user, and document the incident.
Create a new verified restore point after the system is clean.

explanations.task-1: The infection must first be identified.
explanations.task-2: Quarantine limits spread before removal.
explanations.task-3: Updated tools improve detection and cleanup.
explanations.task-4: Repair and patching address residual risk.
explanations.task-6: A clean restore point provides a safe recovery baseline.

missions.title: Harden the Traveling Fleet
missions.objective: 220-1202 2.7, 2.8, and 2.11 — Endpoint, mobile, and browser security
missions.briefing: Match each exposure to the most direct hardening action.
instructions: Review every task.
Select the best response for each task.
Each correct task earns one point.

tasks.prompt: A laptop permits unlimited failed sign-in attempts.
A managed phone containing business mail is reported missing.
A browser permits unapproved extensions from any source.
Workstations continue using unsupported software versions.
Sensitive browser sessions remain active after shared-device use.

options.label: Issue managed remote lock or wipe
End sessions and clear sensitive browser data

explanations.task-1: Lockout slows repeated password guessing.
explanations.task-2: Managed lock or wipe protects data on a missing phone.
explanations.task-3: Extension control prevents unauthorized add-ons.
explanations.task-4: Supported patched software reduces known vulnerability exposure.
explanations.task-5: Ending sessions prevents the next user from inheriting access.

missions.title: Retire the Records Vault
missions.briefing: Assign the approved disposal method to each storage case.
instructions: Review every task.
Select the best response for each task.
Each correct task earns one point.

tasks.prompt: A reusable encrypted SSD leaves the department but remains company property.
A failed magnetic hard disk held highly sensitive records and cannot be reused.
Paper forms contain customer identifiers.
A working magnetic disk will be reassigned internally after approved sanitization.
A damaged flash device cannot be securely erased.

explanations.task-1: Cryptographic erase can rapidly render encrypted SSD data inaccessible.
explanations.task-2: A failed sensitive disk requires documented destruction.
explanations.task-3: Cross-cut shredding destroys paper records.
explanations.task-4: Approved overwriting prepares working magnetic media for reuse.
explanations.task-5: Unreliable flash media must be destroyed when secure erase cannot be verified.

missions.title: Read the Boot Omens
missions.briefing: Classify the most likely Windows failure from each symptom set.
instructions: Review every task.
Select the best response for each task.
Each correct task earns one point.

tasks.prompt: A system loops immediately after a newly installed driver loads.
Only one user receives temporary-profile notices; other accounts work.
Disk usage remains at 100 percent and the system responds slowly.
An update repeatedly rolls back during restart.

explanations.task-1: Failure beginning with a driver installation implicates that driver.
explanations.task-2: A single affected account points to profile corruption.
explanations.task-3: Sustained disk saturation explains system-wide delay.
explanations.task-4: Repeated rollback is an update installation failure.

missions.title: Restore the Broken Startup Chain
missions.briefing: Order a least-disruptive startup repair.
instructions: Review every task.
Select the best response for each task.
Each correct task earns one point.

tasks.prompt: Record the startup symptom and recent changes.
Enter the recovery environment and run startup diagnostics.
Attempt the least disruptive correction, such as removing the recent driver or update.
Use broader repair or restore options only if the targeted correction fails.
Restart repeatedly, validate applications and data, and document the result.

explanations.task-1: Evidence collection protects diagnosis.
explanations.task-2: Recovery diagnostics provide controlled access.
explanations.task-3: Targeted rollback minimizes impact.
explanations.task-4: Broader recovery follows failed narrow repair.

missions.title: Repair the Mobile Application Fleet
missions.briefing: Match each mobile symptom to its safest initial correction.
instructions: Review every task.
Select the best response for each task.
Each correct task earns one point.

tasks.prompt: One application cannot use the camera after a privacy-setting change.
An application crashes after its cached data becomes corrupted.
A vendor fixed a known application defect in the current release.
A nonessential application remains unstable after settings and updates are verified.

explanations.task-1: Camera access is controlled by application permissions.
explanations.task-2: Clearing cache removes disposable corrupted state.
explanations.task-3: Installing the fixed release addresses the known defect.
explanations.task-4: Reinstallation replaces damaged program files after safer checks.

missions.title: Contain the Lost Mobile Device
missions.briefing: Sequence the response to a missing managed phone.
instructions: Review every task.
Select the best response for each task.
Each correct task earns one point.

tasks.prompt: Confirm ownership, last known use, and the incident report.
Revoke active sessions and sensitive tokens according to policy.
Use management tools to locate and remotely lock the device.
Escalate to an approved wipe if recovery fails and policy conditions are met.
Document actions, restore the user on a replacement, and review the incident.

explanations.task-1: Verification prevents action against the wrong asset.
explanations.task-2: Revocation limits account exposure.
explanations.task-3: Location and lock protect data while preserving recovery.
explanations.task-4: Wipe is an escalated destructive control.
explanations.task-5: Documentation and restoration complete the response.

missions.title: Diagnose the Compromised Office
missions.briefing: Classify each correlated indicator set.
instructions: Review every task.
Select the best response for each task.
Each correct task earns one point.

tasks.prompt: Browser searches redirect, an unknown proxy appears, and extensions return after removal.
Security tools stop, files receive new extensions, and a payment note appears.
A new local administrator exists and remote sign-ins occur overnight.
Users see pop-ups from an installed program that also changes the home page.

explanations.task-1: Persistent proxy and extension changes indicate browser hijacking.
explanations.task-2: Encrypted files and extortion identify ransomware.
explanations.task-3: An unauthorized administrator plus remote activity indicates account compromise.
explanations.task-4: Bundled advertising and browser changes are typical of a potentially unwanted program.

missions.title: Recover the Mixed-Platform Outpost
missions.briefing: Select the first diagnosis, containment action, recovery path, and validation target for each incident.
instructions: Review each requirement.
Select every configuration field.
Each correct field earns partial credit.

tasks.label: Windows boot
tasks.prompt: A driver update causes a repeatable startup crash; data remains intact.

tasks.label: Managed tablet
tasks.prompt: A tablet is missing with active business sessions.

tasks.label: Office PC
tasks.prompt: Files are encrypted and a ransom notice is visible.

explanations.task-1: The repeatable post-driver crash calls for controlled rollback and boot validation.
explanations.task-2: The lost managed device requires session protection, remote control, and compliance validation.
explanations.task-3: Ransomware requires isolation, clean recovery, and integrity verification.

missions.title: Route the Support Records
missions.objective: 220-1202 4.1–4.2 — Documentation, support systems, and change management
missions.briefing: Classify each record by its proper support-system destination.
instructions: Review every task.
Select the best response for each task.
Each correct task earns one point.

tasks.prompt: A user reports a single application failure and receives a case number.
A laptop serial number, owner, and warranty date are updated.
A proven repair procedure is prepared for future technicians.
A firewall modification requires impact analysis and approval.

explanations.task-1: An individual service interruption belongs in an incident ticket.
explanations.task-2: Ownership and warranty data belong in the asset record.
explanations.task-3: Reusable verified procedures belong in the knowledge base.
explanations.task-4: Planned infrastructure modification requires change control.

missions.title: Restore the Archive After the Flood
missions.briefing: Order the recovery of a damaged file server.
instructions: Review every task.
Select the best response for each task.
Each correct task earns one point.

tasks.prompt: Confirm the incident scope and protect the damaged source from further writes.
Select the approved recovery point and verify backup integrity.
Restore the full backup to isolated replacement storage.
Apply the required incremental backups in chronological order.
Validate files and permissions, obtain owner acceptance, and return the service.
Document recovery time, data loss, and corrective actions.

explanations.task-1: Protecting evidence and remaining data comes first.
explanations.task-2: The chosen restore source must be verified.
explanations.task-3: The full backup establishes the base.
explanations.task-4: Incrementals are applied in their dependency order.

missions.title: Inspect the Safe Repair Bay
missions.briefing: Identify four safety and environmental-control areas in the original Hydra repair-bay diagram.
instructions: Study the original Hydra diagram.
Select the best label for every callout.
Each correct callout earns one point.

tasks.prompt: Identify the ESD-controlled workbench.
Identify the isolated battery container.
Identify the ventilated service enclosure.
Identify the electronics recycling station.

explanations.task-1: The grounded mat and wrist connection mark the ESD bench.
explanations.task-2: The fire-resistant marked container isolates damaged batteries.
explanations.task-3: The extraction hood provides ventilation for approved service work.
explanations.task-4: The labeled collection bin separates electronic waste.

missions.title: Conduct the Privacy-Safe Remote Session
missions.objective: 220-1202 4.6, 4.7, and 4.9 — Privacy, professionalism, and remote access
missions.briefing: Match each remote-support event to the correct professional response.
instructions: Review every task.
Select the best response for each task.
Each correct task earns one point.

tasks.prompt: Before connecting, the technician cannot verify the caller or device owner.
Private customer records appear while screen sharing is active.
The user becomes frustrated and interrupts troubleshooting.
The repair is complete but the unattended remote agent remains installed.
Potentially prohibited material appears in a folder unrelated to the reported issue.

options.label: Stop sharing and protect private information
Use calm questions and confirm understanding
End the session and remove unauthorized persistence
Stop unnecessary inspection and follow reporting policy

explanations.task-1: Identity and authorization must precede remote access.
explanations.task-2: Screen sharing should stop when private information is exposed.
explanations.task-3: Professional communication keeps the user informed and the session productive.
explanations.task-4: Remote persistence must match authorization and policy.
explanations.task-5: Technicians should avoid unnecessary access and follow organizational reporting rules.

missions.title: Govern the Automation Oracle
missions.objective: 220-1202 4.2, 4.8, and 4.10 — Change management, scripting, and AI fundamentals
missions.briefing: Sequence the controlled introduction of an AI-assisted support script.
instructions: Review every task.
Select the best response for each task.
Each correct task earns one point.

tasks.prompt: Define the support problem, allowed data, success criteria, and human owner.
Design the script logic with validated inputs, safe conditions, logging, and error handling.
Test deterministic script behavior and independently verify AI-generated recommendations with synthetic data.
Submit risks, test evidence, rollback steps, and privacy controls for approval.
Deploy to a limited group with monitoring and a ready rollback path.
Review outputs, failures, bias or hallucination indicators, and user feedback before expansion.

explanations.task-1: Scope and ownership define safe use.
explanations.task-2: Input validation and error handling make automation predictable.
explanations.task-3: AI output requires independent verification in testing.
explanations.task-4: Approval depends on evidence and rollback planning.
explanations.task-6: Ongoing human review detects unreliable output before broader use.
